variables.policy_prompt_for_subgoal: An episode starts in subgoal A. Rules: 1. If the scene shows no peg held in the gripper (no 'is held in the gripper' entry, fingers 100% open, gripper raised out of frame) and the demonstration steps are shown with an empty memory: choose A, pick up the peg by grasping one end, and point at grasp_point, i.e. the coordinates of the peg end that the demonstration gripper closed on, as that end appears in the current scene. Write grasp_point and insert_side at this step. 2. If the scene shows a peg end 'is held in the gripper' (fingers about 22-25% open, gripper raised): the pick is done. If insert_side is right, choose B, insert the peg from the right side. If insert_side is left, choose C, insert the peg from the left side. 3. If the scene shows no peg held and the memory already holds grasp_point (the pick failed or dropped): choose A again and point at grasp_point, using the current position of the peg head or peg tail entry in the current scene nearest that stored point, whatever its class. 4. Any situation not covered: if nothing is held, choose A pointing at grasp_point (or, if grasp_point is unknown, at the peg end nearest the box); if something is held, choose B when insert_side is right or unknown, and C when insert_side is left. Carry grasp_point and insert_side forward unchanged.

fields.name: grasp_point
fields.description: At the first decision step (demonstration shown, memory empty): find the demonstration frame where the gripper is at its lowest height (about 0.01-0.03) and the fingers have just gone from 100% open to about 22-25% open; pick the peg head or peg tail entry whose coordinates are nearest the gripper in that frame; then write that same end's coordinates as they appear in the start-of-execution scene (pegs are at their demonstration t=0 positions). At every later step copy the carried value unchanged, even once a peg is held. The end's class is not written; when it is needed, read it as whichever class ('peg head' or 'peg tail') lists these coordinates in the scene. e.g. [114, 212]
fields.annotation: The [y, x] of the peg end the demonstration gripper closed on. Set at the first decision step from the demonstration frame where the gripper is at its lowest (height about 0.01-0.03) and the fingers first drop from 100% open to the closed-on-peg width (about 22-25% open): take the peg head or peg tail entry nearest the gripper position in that frame, and record that end's coordinates as they appear in the start-of-execution scene (the pegs lie at the same positions as at demonstration t=0). Never changes afterwards, even once a peg is held. Whether that end is a head or a tail is not stored; it is whichever class ('peg head' or 'peg tail') lists those coordinates in the scene. e.g. [114, 212]

fields.name: insert_side
fields.description: At the first decision step: look at the last few demonstration frames, where the gripper is low (height about 0.04), fingers still closed, and gripper y close to the aperture box y. If the gripper x in those frames is SMALLER than the aperture box x, write right; if LARGER, write left. At every later step copy the carried value unchanged. e.g. right
fields.annotation: The side of the box the demonstration inserted the peg from, right or left. Set at the first decision step from the final demonstration frames (gripper low, height about 0.04, fingers still closed, gripper y near the aperture box y): if the gripper x there is SMALLER than the aperture box x the value is right; if LARGER it is left. Never changes afterwards. e.g. right
